fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s Ember 8 recorded 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year, above the discussed 8/100,000 threshold.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 5 business days after learning of it; incidents involving death, serious injury, or an active risk to the public must be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that determination.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model shall undergo sustained-heat testing at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model. Manufacturers shall provide complete per-model results, including protocol, sample size, and failure rate, to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy or are considering buying that model; results may not be withheld from those customers as confidential. Exceeding 5% alone shall not automatically require withdrawal from the market; continued sale during remediation is subject to regulator-approved controls and timely retesting.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new home battery units placed on the market after adoption shall support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers shall equip previously installed units with this capability, or provide an equivalent regulator-approved emergency isolation measure, within 6 years after adoption.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units placed on the market shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Manufacturers shall provide customers clear safety notices about material risks, relevant incidents, and protective actions promptly, and no later than 5 business days after determining a material safety risk. A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; manufacturers shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and initiate the recall, including instructions for safe shutdown, repair, replacement, or refund.

document.section_notes: The final rules are mostly strict on reporting, testing, and recall triggers: all incidents reportable, 55°C/5% testing, mandatory recall at 8/100k. However, S2 allows continued sale during a regulator-set remediation timetable without a fixed end or interim cap, and S3 gives a long 6-year retrofit deadline. S4 and S5 include Halcyon's 36-month suppression phase-in and 5-business-day customer notices, but S5 lacks a mandatory serious-injury recall clause.
